newsitem.title: USA: One cadet punished for displaying swastika.
newsitem.headline: One cadet punished for displaying swastika.

text.p: Officials at the Citadel said Tuesday the state-funded military college punished one cadet during the past academic year for displaying what appeared to be a swastika on a piece of cardboard.

"The Citadel categorically denies that it now condones or ever has condoned the display of Nazi emblems or regalia anywhere on campus," Major General Roger Poole, the Citadel's interim president, said in a statement.

The South Carolina school, which waged a lengthy legal fight against co-education, has been the subject of scrutiny since December, when two of the first women enrolled in the formerly all-male institution withdrew and alleged they had been subjected to physical abuse and sexual harassment.
Fourteen male cadets were punished in the wake of the allegations, including two who were dismissed and three who resigned.
This week, two former male cadets said in court papers that the two women, Jeanie Mentavlos and Kim Messer, were assigned to Echo company, a group in which they said cadets glorified Nazi symbols.
The Citadel denied the allegations and said the one cadet who was punished was not a member of Echo company.

The Citadel also said that Craig Belsole and Dan Eggers, the two men who leveled the accusations, had been punished for failure to report the hazing and noted that they made their allegations as part of a motion to stop the Citadel's efforts to obtain documents connected with an FBI investigation of hazing at the college.

"The entire motion is a move on the part of Mr. Belsole and Mr. Eggers to protect themselves from additional punishment during the period from March 10 through the end of the college year. The statements lack any basis in fact," Poole said.
He said he has also directed school officials to investigate all cadet mottos, creeds and related items and provide a report by Sept. 1.
